facts.label: F1
facts.text:
[F1] The basic module in the symmetric-group convention is
$M_{\mathrm{sym}} = J^{-1}V(\Lambda_0) = J^{-1}M_{\mathrm{QG}}$, its crystal is
the empty component and its labels are exactly the $3$-restricted partitions;
$(4)$ is not $3$-restricted and $(4)' = (1,1,1,1)$ is not $3$-regular
([[thm-restricted-partition-component-is-the-basic-crystal-in-the-symmetric-group-convention]],
[[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]]).

consuming_steps.claim: The two finite checks. The shape $(4)$ is not $3$-restricted, because $\lambda_1 - \lambda_2 = 4 - 0 = 4 \ge 3$; its conjugate is $(1,1,1,1)$ (four columns of height one), not $(1,1,1)$, and it is not $3$-regular because the positive part $1$ occurs four times, and $4 \ge 3$. By [F1], therefore, neither $(4)$ nor $(1,1,1,1)$ is a label of the basic component in its respective convention: $(4)$ is not a basic label in the symmetric-group model, and $(1,1,1,1)$ is not an $e$-regular label on the quantum-group side.

Transport to the symmetric-group convention. Applying $J^{-1}$ to the field module $M$ gives $M_{\mathrm{sym}} = J^{-1}M$, and $J^{-1}|1111\rangle = M_{(1111)'} = M_{(4)}$; since $J^{-1}$ is a linear isomorphism, $M_{(4)} = J^{-1}|1111\rangle \notin M_{\mathrm{sym}}$ by step 2.1, and likewise $G_{\mathrm{sym}}(4) = J^{-1}G(1111) \notin M_{\mathrm{sym}}$ by step 3.1. Since also $M_{(4)} \in F_{\mathrm{sym}}$, the transported full Fock space is strictly larger than its cyclic basic module, refuting the false statement.

The full signature remains meaningful on these shapes. At $(4)$ the corners are the removable node $(1,4)$ of residue $3 \equiv 0$ and the addable nodes $(1,5)$ of residue $4 \equiv 1$ and $(2,1)$ of residue $-1 \equiv 2$; the residue-$0$ word is the single $-$, so the modular signature has good node $(1,4)$ and $\tilde e_0(4) = (3)$, an edge of the full transported crystal. Both $(4)$ and $(3)$ are non-$3$-restricted, so this edge joins two vertices of other components, not a route into the empty component, in agreement with the component identification of [F1]; modular signature statements restricted to restricted labels do not apply to $(4)$ as a basic label.

consuming_steps.claim: **The graded composition series.** Multiplication by $t$ raises the degree by $\deg t=2$ in the transported grading, so $tP\cong D\{2\}$ and $P\cong D\oplus D\{2\}$ as graded vector spaces; hence the graded composition series is $0\subset tP\subset P$ with $[P]=(1+q^2)[D]$ in $G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1})$, which is not a shift of $[D]$ [F2, F4].

**Specht degrees and Fock data.** The unique tableau of shape $(2)$ has degree $d_A(2)=1$ (the addable $1$-node $(2,1)$ lies strictly below the removable node $(1,2)$, and there is no removable $1$-node below it), and the unique tableau of $(1,1)$ has degree $0$; hence $[S(2)]=q[D]$ and $[S(1,1)]=[D]$ [F3]. The recorded $e=2$ Fock computation gives $G(1,1)=M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)}$ and $G^*(1,1)=(M_{1,1}+qM_{(2)})/(1+q^2)$, so $G(1,1)=(1+q^2)G^*(1,1)$ [F3].

**The identifications and the pairing.** By [F4] the projective class $[P]$ corresponds to $G(1,1)$ and the simple class $[D]$ to $G^*(1,1)$, giving $[P]=(1+q^2)[D]\mapsto G(1,1)$ and $[D]\mapsto G^*(1,1)$ under the transported identifications. The graded Cartan pairing is read from $\operatorname{Hom}^0(P,D)=\mathbb C$ and $\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}(P,P)=1+q^2$ (endomorphisms are the identity and multiplication by $t$, of degree $2$), so $h([P],[D])=1$ and $h([P],[P])=1+q^2$; the graded composition multiplicity is $[P:D]_q=1+q^2$ with ungraded value $2$ [F4]. Hence the projective class is not a simple class, and the projective and simple families are dual but not equal [F4].

**Choice.** The computation uses the explicit two-dimensional algebra, its two partitions and the recorded $e=2$ polynomials; no family of nonempty sets is selected, so choice is inherited only through the transported identifications cited in [F4].

consuming_steps.claim: **The restricted coefficient matrix is dominance-unitriangular.** Fix a content, and take the square minor $D_{\mathrm{res}}$ with rows and columns the restricted labels and row-$\mu$, column-$\lambda$ entry $d_{(\lambda,\mu)}$. By [F2], the diagonal is $1$ and the only off-diagonal support has $\mu$ strictly dominating $\lambda$. Choose a finite linear order refining this dominance direction; then $D_{\mathrm{res}}=I+N$ is triangular with nilpotent $N$ and coefficients in $\mathbb Z[q]$, and $(I+N)^{-1}=\sum_{k\ge0}(-N)^k$ is a finite polynomial matrix. In particular $\det D_{\mathrm{res}}=1$ and the minor is invertible over $A$.

**The restricted form is nondegenerate.** Let $D$ be the rectangular matrix with all standard rows and restricted lower columns on the fixed content. The Gram matrix is $H=D^{\mathsf t}D$ by [F1]. By [F2] its columns at $q=0$ are distinct coordinate vectors, so $H(0)=I$ and $\det H(0)=1$. Thus $H$ is invertible over $\mathbb Q(q)$; the form on the basic subspace is nondegenerate and identifies its field dual with that subspace.

**Expansion in the dual upper vectors.** Put $v:=\sum_{\lambda}d_{(\lambda,\mu)}G^*(\lambda)$, a finite sum over the restricted labels of the content [F3]. Using the duality $B(G(\lambda),G^*(\lambda'))=\delta_{\lambda\lambda'}$ from [F3] and step 3.1, for every restricted $\lambda'$ $$B(v,G(\lambda'))=\sum_\lambda d_{(\lambda,\mu)}B(G^*(\lambda),G(\lambda'))=d_{(\lambda',\mu)}=\operatorname{Std}_\mu(G(\lambda')),$$ and both sides are bilinear in their arguments, so $B(v,x)=\operatorname{Std}_\mu(x)$ for all $x\in V$. By uniqueness in step 3.1, $v=\pi(M_\mu)$, which is the displayed expansion.

**Upper dual basis and the failure of lower integrality.** The matrix expressing the restricted family $\{\operatorname{Std}_\lambda\}$ in the restricted dual family $\{G^*(\lambda)\}$ is the transpose of $D_{\mathrm{res}}$ of step 1.1, hence unitriangular over $A$ with unit diagonal; therefore the restricted $\operatorname{Std}_\lambda$ form an $A$-basis of the upper dual lattice and the full ambient family may be redundant [F2, F3]. The coefficients $d_{(\lambda,\mu)}$ are Laurent polynomials, but $\pi$ need not preserve the lower integral lattice: in $e=2$, at the content of the two-part partition $2$, the recorded transition data give $G_{11}=M_{11}+qM_2$, whose dual-form upper vector is $G^*_{11}=(M_{11}+qM_2)/(1+q^2)$ and hence $\operatorname{Std}_{11}=\pi(M_{11})=(M_{11}+qM_2)/(1+q^2)$ has the genuine field denominator $1+q^2$, which is not a unit of $A$; the raw standard vector $M_{11}$ is nevertheless an ambient lattice basis vector.

**The canonical recursion, finiteness and Choice.** All sums at fixed content are finite. The form identification of [F3] gives $B(F_ix,y)=B(x,q^{-1}K_iE_iy)$, and both $V$ and $V^\perp$ are stable under the quantum action: for $x\in V^\perp$ and $y\in V$, contravariance gives $B(ux,y)=B(x,\sigma(u)y)=0$. Hence the orthogonal projection $\pi$ commutes with the action. In the symmetric linear-$J$ model, conjugating the QG diagram changes lower-content nodes to above nodes and reflects colors; the transported removal formula is therefore $E_iM_\mu=\sum_{A\ \mathrm{removable}}q^{-d^A(\mu)}M_{\mu\setminus A}$, where $d^A$ is the addable-minus-removable count strictly above $A$ in the smaller diagram. Applying $\pi$ gives the same recursion for $\operatorname{Std}_\mu$, as used by the later Specht comparison. No new choice is made; [C1] is inherited.

facts.label: F2
facts.text:
[F2] The Fock model has nodes with residues $c-r$, standard vectors $M_\mu$ for
all partitions, and node action formulas satisfying the quantum affine
relations ([[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]],
[[def-level-one-partition-fock-space-and-node-residues]],
[[lem-semi-infinite-wedges-are-indexed-by-partitions-and-give-node-action-formulas]],
[[thm-the-fock-space-node-formulas-satisfy-the-quantum-affine-relations]]); the
projection $\pi$ onto the basic module commutes with the field quantum action
and satisfies $E_iM_\mu=\sum_Aq^{-d^A(\mu\setminus A)}M_{\mu\setminus A}$, where
$d^A$ is the number of addable $i$-nodes strictly above $A$ minus the number of
removable $i$-nodes strictly above $A$, computed in $\mu\setminus A$
([[lem-standard-fock-vectors-expand-in-the-upper-global-basis]]).

consuming_steps.claim: **The identical standard-coordinate evaluation.** If $A$ is a removable $i$-node of $\mu$ and $\alpha=\operatorname{cont}(\mu)$, the Fock formula [F2] gives its removal coefficient $q^{-d^A(\mu\setminus A)}$. The operator $K_i$ on the resulting weight $\Lambda_0-\alpha+\alpha_i$ multiplies by $q^{h_i(\alpha)+2}$. Contravariance of [F3] therefore gives the coefficient of $M_\mu$ in $F_iM_{\mu\setminus A}$ as $q^{h_i(\alpha)+1-d^A(\mu\setminus A)}=q^{d_A(\mu)}$, by [F4]. Iterating additions from the vacuum enumerates precisely the standard tableaux of shape $\mu$ with successive residues $\mathbf i$: at each stage the occupied nodes form a partition, and conversely its increasing filling records the addition path. The product of the node factors is $q^{\sum_A d_A}=q^{\deg T}$ by the degree recursion. Hence the coordinate functional $\operatorname{Std}_\mu(x)=B(x,M_\mu)$ satisfies $\operatorname{Std}_\mu(F_{i_d}\cdots F_{i_1}v_{\Lambda_0})=\sum_{T:i_T=\mathbf i}q^{\deg T}$, exactly step 1.1.

**Equality in the restricted integral dual.** The basic highest-weight module over $\mathbb Q(q)$ is generated from the vacuum by the negative generators, so its vectors $F_{i_d}\cdots F_{i_1}v_{\Lambda_0}$ span every weight space; no assertion that ordinary words alone span the divided-power lattice over $A$ is needed. Steps 1.1–2.1 make the two functionals equal on this field spanning family. Both lie in the restricted integral weight dual by [F1] and the coordinate-functional construction of [F2]; their field equality therefore is equality in that lattice. Under the nondegenerate contravariant form, $\operatorname{Std}_\mu$ is represented by $S_\mu=\pi(M_\mu)$, giving the stated equation. It holds in both field-characteristic branches because the homogeneous basis and integral categorical pairing do, and uses no cellular head classification or characteristic-zero based theorem. Choice is precisely the inherited [C1].

facts.text: [F4] For a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, every $p$-restricted partition is obtained from the empty partition by successive cogood additions, and every nonempty $p$-restricted partition has a good node; the argument is choice-free ([[prop-every-p-restricted-partition-is-reached-by-cogood-node-additions]]).

facts.label: F5
facts.text: [F5] For $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, $\mu$ $p$-restricted and $\varepsilon_i(\mu)>0$, the residue-summand functor $E_i$ of [[def-generalized-jm-primary-idempotents-and-residue-summand-functors]] satisfies $\operatorname{soc} E_iD(\mu) \cong \operatorname{hd} E_iD(\mu) \cong D(\mu \setminus A)$ with $A$ the good $i$-node, and the total multiplicity of $D(\mu\setminus A)$ in $E_iD(\mu)$ is $\varepsilon_i(\mu)$ ([[thm-good-node-gives-the-simple-socle-and-head-of-residue-restriction]]). Here $D(\mu)$ is the simple module of the $p$-restricted label $\mu$ in the dual-Specht convention, and $E_i$ is the projection of the restriction onto the summand whose Jucys-Murphy content ends in $i$; in particular $\operatorname{Res} M = \bigoplus_i E_iM$.

consuming_steps.claim: The transported component is connected and generated from the vacuum. The empty component of [F3] is the canonical $B(\Lambda_0)$, hence connected and generated from its highest vertex by the $\tilde f^{\mathrm{QG}}$; transporting along the bijection of step 1.1, the $e$-restricted labels form one connected component of the transported crystal, generated from the empty partition by the operators $\tilde f^{\mathrm{sym}}_i$, that is, by modular cogood additions. In particular every $e$-restricted shape is reached from the empty partition by successive cogood additions, and dually by successive good deletions; for $e = p$ prime this is also the choice-free statement of [F4], whose good and cogood nodes are the modular ones by [F2].

For part 2, the full $F_{\mathrm{sym}}$ has all partitions as vertices and its module is the transport of the modules of [F3], so its field decomposition is $F_{\mathrm{sym}} \cong \bigoplus_{k\ge0} V(\Lambda_0 - k\delta)^{\oplus p(k)}$ with $p(k)$ ordinary partition numbers; this direct sum is infinite, so $F_{\mathrm{sym}}$ is reducible whenever at least two summands are nonzero (for instance the summands $V(\Lambda_0)$ and $V(\Lambda_0-\delta)$). Since the empty component is exactly the $e$-restricted shapes by step 3.1, every other vertex of the full crystal is a non-restricted shape, and conversely each non-restricted shape lies outside the empty component. The axiom of choice is inherited through [F3], both here for the field decomposition and in steps 1.1-2.1 for the canonical highest-weight-crystal identification. The transport itself introduces no choice. The vertex-set identification and reachability can also be read directly from the choice-free partition-graph supplier of [F2], and [F4] gives the prime-case reachability without choice.

Part 3, the James labels and the socle formula. Let $k$ be of characteristic $p > 0$ and $e = p$; $e$-restricted $\lambda$ are exactly the labels $D(\lambda)$ of the simple $kS_d$-modules in the dual-Specht convention, and for $p$-regular $\lambda'$ the published dictionary gives $D^{\lambda'} \cong D(\lambda) \otimes \operatorname{sgn}$ by [F6]. Suppose $\varepsilon_i(\lambda) > 0$ and let $A$ be the good $i$-node, so that $\tilde e_i\lambda = \lambda \setminus A$ and, by [F5], $\operatorname{soc} E_iD(\lambda) \cong D(\lambda\setminus A)$. Tensoring with $\operatorname{sgn}$ negates the Jucys-Murphy action: for $v \otimes w$ in $M \otimes \operatorname{sgn}$, $L_r(v\otimes w) = \sum_{s<r}((s\,r)v) \otimes ((s\,r)w) = -L_r v \otimes w$ because each $(s\,r)$ acts by $-1$ on $\operatorname{sgn}$ by [F6]; hence the content vector of the sign twist is the negative, and by [F5] the residue summands satisfy $E_{-i}\bigl(M \otimes \operatorname{sgn}\bigr) \cong (E_iM) \otimes \operatorname{sgn}$. The twist is an exact invertible endofunctor (its square is the identity on isomorphism classes), so it preserves socles and simples; applying it to $\operatorname{soc} E_iD(\lambda) \cong D(\lambda\setminus A)$ gives $\operatorname{soc}\bigl(E_{-i}(D(\lambda)\otimes\operatorname{sgn})\bigr) \cong D(\lambda\setminus A) \otimes \operatorname{sgn}$, and the two published re-identifications $D(\lambda)\otimes\operatorname{sgn} \cong D^{\lambda'}$ and $D(\lambda\setminus A)\otimes\operatorname{sgn} \cong D^{(\lambda\setminus A)'}$ of [F6] yield $\operatorname{soc} E_{-i}D^{\lambda'} \cong D^{(\tilde e_i\lambda)'}$; this is the stated formula, and it exhibits $E_{-i}$ as the sign twist of the residue functor $E_i$.
